News.title: First victim of Golders Green terror attack is pictured with pals saying ‘nicest guy’ would ‘never hurt a fly’
News.content:
STAB BRAVERY First victim of Golders Green terror attack is pictured with pals saying ‘nicest guy’ would ‘never hurt a fly’

ONE of the victims of the horrific terror attack in Golders Green earlier today was the nicest guy” who “wouldn’t hurt a fly” as he is pictured for the first time.

Friends of Moshe Shine told The Sun the broad daylight stabbing has filled the community with “horror”.





The 76-year-old was “waiting to go home by bus at the bus stop” when he was attacked a member of the Jewish community said.

A friend of Moshe said he was “He’s very softly spoken. Very generous. He’s a very nice, smiley guy.

“Really the nicest guy. He never lost his temper or raised his voice.”

The friend of Moshe’s, who wishes to remain anonymous, said: “I have spoken to his nephew and he was the one who told me that he is in a serious condition.



“One of his wounds is very serious, I think it was in the neck.”

They continued: ““We are not really feeling safe in the country at the moment.

“It’s purely antisemitic, I know it’s the first time they’ve actually classified it as a terrorist attack but we think they all the attacks are terrorist attacks.

“We’re only being attacked because we are Jewish, simple as that.

“Forget this issue about Israel, it’s got nothing to do with Israel. It’s the fact that we are Jewish.



“It’s just basic antisemitism.”

News.title: Royal gifts for Trump carry diplomatic price tag — and a clear message on Nato, Ukraine & the environment
News.content:
YOU can imagine the delight when the official in charge of sourcing a vital gift from the King heard about the bell.

After somehow locating it from a 1940s Australian submarine, not only did it have the word TRUMP emblazoned across it… but it was gold, to boot.





And the message it came with struck the perfect note: when America needs Britain, “just give us a ring”.

That sums up the meticulous thought and planning that has gone into this sophisticated Royal love-bombing of a leader clearly susceptible to charm.

From joking about the new ballroom being akin to us burning down the White House in 1814, to a gentle chiding about Trump’s World War Two comments, the King’s toast to the President on Tuesday hit the spot.

But the jokes and gifts came with a price tag.



There was no escaping the rebuke on the importance of Nato and standing by Ukraine.

And it would not have been a speech from King Charles without a little lecture on the environment, even if some Republicans rolled their eyes at his rhetoric.



The speech had something for everyone, with Democrats particularly liking the history lesson on how our Magna Carta is still used to check American power.

But it was the deftness of hand that only the King has made this intervention so successful.

Not a wagging finger in sight.



Instead, a powerful punch wrapped up in a big bow.

News.title: Girl, 5, ‘killed by mother and step-dad was buried alive’ in concrete-covered grave in back yard of her house
News.content:
SICK PARENTS Girl, 5, ‘killed by mother and step-dad was buried alive’ in concrete-covered grave in back yard of her house

A FIVE-YEAR-OLD girl allegedly killed by her mum and stepdad was buried alive, a forensics report suggests.

Maria Clara Aguirre Lisboa’s body was found in a concrete-covered grave behind the house she shared with her mum Luiza Aguirre Barbosa da Silva and her stepdad Rodrigo Ribeiro Machado, west of Sao Paulo.





The autopsy report said she died while being buried alive, with soil found in her windpipe.

It also described trauma to the girl’s head, suggesting that she had been assaulted.

Maria Clara’s body was found October 14, 2025, but investigators think she was murdered around 20 days before the horrifying discovery.

Da Silva and Machado reportedly confessed to the girl’s killing and have been charged with murder with aggravating factors and concealment of a body.

Maria Clara was reported missing by her grandad in early October.

Child Protective Services said they had already been monitoring the little girl’s case, as her stepdad had allegedly threatened her just months before her murder.



Police found her body on October 14, saying it was already in an advanced state of decomposition.

Cops uncovered chilling audio messages to Maria Clara’s dad from her stepdad Machado during the investigation.

The twisted alleged killer urged Maria Clara’s dad to stop “bothering” him and his partner for information about the girl.



In one message, cops say he raved: “Mate, are you deaf as well or something?

“Don’t wind me up, mate.

“I’ve already told you your daughter’s dead. She doesn’t even exist any more.

Stop messing me about, all right? Stop sending me messages, yeah?”

Machado, who has a criminal record, is accused of physical and psychological abuse of Maria Clara and her mum Da Silva, lead investigator Franco Augusto said.



Augusto alleged Da Silva also abused her daughter.

Child protective services said they had not been able to contact Maria Clara’s mum for two months before the girl was reported missing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Maria Clara’s aunt said when the girl’s body was found: “My heart is in pieces knowing that your life was taken in such a cruel and unjust way.”

The accused mum and stepdad will appear in court on May.

News.title: I’ve had death threats & vile abuse for 9yrs as I hunt fugitive £4bn Cryptoqueen – here’s how I KNOW she’s still alive
News.content:
SHE was the glamorous businesswoman who promised investors huge returns on cryptocurrency products – then vanished, taking almost $4billion of their money with her.

Nearly nine years after she was last seen on a Ryanair flight to Athens, in October 2017, Dr Ruja Ignatova — founder of fraudulent crypto scheme OneCoin — is the only woman on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list, with a $5million reward on her head.



And no one wants to see her brought to justice more than brave Scot Jennifer McAdam, who has spent a decade fighting on behalf of the conwoman’s victims, amid chilling death threats, vile abuse and exhausting legal fights that have left her emotionally bruised.

Jennifer came across German- Bulgarian Ignatova in 2016, while looking to invest the modest inheritance her beloved dad had left her.

Nicknamed the Cryptoqueen, Ignatova had mansions in ­Bulgaria, Germany and the Middle East, London offices overlooking Hyde Park, plus a penthouse in Kensington stuffed with artwork including Andy Warhol originals, as well as owning a superyacht named Davina, after her daughter.



Inspired by Ignatova’s talks at top financial summits, Jennifer invested 10,000 euros (£8,700) and persuaded family and friends to do the same — to the tune of 250,000 euros (£217,000).



Her own investment grew to £100,000, but when she tried to withdraw some cash to repair a broken fridge, she found she couldn’t. Pressure from OneCoin followed — Jennifer was told she would be foolish to withdraw while it was rising in value.

Chopped up

Eventually she went to the City of London police, who told her they believed it to be an investment scam known as a Ponzi scheme, and that it was under investigation.

Jennifer told The Sun: “I’ll never get the words to describe that feeling when you realise it’s a fraud, that all of that money was gone and was never coming back.

“My knees went from under me and I fell to the floor. It was like a tornado ripping through me, and I was absolutely numb.”

Jennifer was one of millions of victims worldwide, including 70,000 Brits who lost a total of £100million.



When police dropped the investigation for “lack of evidence”, a frustrated Jennifer took to social media to warn others about Ignatova, who was still drumming up business around the world.

Then seven months later, the Cryptoqueen vanished.

Jennifer said: “I was so angry, because I always felt that would happen. I felt that there had been a chance to get her and now she’s gone.

“She’s got all the victims’ money and when you’re that rich, you can hide for a very long time.”

The mystery inspired the 2019 BBC podcast The Missing Cryptoqueen, and four new episodes released earlier this year investigated further reported sightings of Ignatova.



Theories range from one based on a 2023 reported sighting in South Africa to rumours that she was dismembered and thrown overboard from a yacht.

But Jennifer firmly believes she is alive, and said: “It’s bulls**t. She is the most amazing storyteller, so when the Bulgarian media said, ‘She’s been chopped up and thrown over the side of a yacht’, I thought, ‘That’s what they want you to believe’.

“It’s easy for her to get that story out and it takes the pressure off. Shortly after that, the FBI upped the reward from $250,000 to $5million. They don’t go after dead dogs. They know she’s alive.”

Then came the threats. Jennifer said: “Initially it was death threats, then it went to sexual threats. They were posting videos of disgusting things on our groups.

I’ll never get the words to describe that feeling when you realise it’s a fraud, that all of that money was gone and was never coming back Jennifer McAdam

“Because I invested my late dad’s inheritance, one said, ‘F* you and your dead daddy’. My phones have been hacked so I’ve had to regularly change phones and numbers.”



In 2017 OneCoin sent a defamation letter — also known as a cease-and-desist letter — to Jennifer’s home, revealing they knew her address.

She said: “I would keep the blinds closed all day because I was terrified. I don’t sleep at night.

“Victims who speak out and own their homes can’t afford to come up against these powerful law firms because rich clients can keep it going while you’re buried.

“But I wouldn’t be silenced because I didn’t own my house so I didn’t have that fear that it could get taken away. In 2023 the calls started again on a new number.

“The first one was a video to WhatsApp of a guy pleasuring himself, saying what he’d do to me.



“They started ringing at three o’clock in the morning until 10am, an Eastern European voice, leaving voice notes about what he was going to do to me.”

In one video sent to Jennifer and seen by The Sun, OneCoin executive Cordel King Jayms fires a machine gun, with the caption: “Pretending I see the OneLife haters”.



Jennifer said: “My house is like Fort Knox, with security cameras and locks. It’s in the US Department of Justice files that Ruja is connected to Eastern European criminal networks, Mafia, so you don’t take that lightly.”

Hope came in 2023 when a major London law firm offered to take on a class action lawsuit against individuals connected to the scam.

But funding was pulled just a month before the court date, leaving victims at risk of massive legal costs.

Jennifer said: “As a victim of fraud, you’re already wiped out financially, and again, the only blessing was that I didn’t own my house.”



Film deal

Eventually lawyers Genevieve Quierin, Tim Knight, Stephen Littleford and Phoebe Love, from law firm Stephenson Harwood, and KCs Patrick Green and Kathleen Donnelly, who worked on the infamous Post Office scandal case, stepped in and worked for free to make sure the victims didn’t have to pay any costs. They are now looking at whether any more legal avenues are available.

Jennifer has even signed a film deal, with Kate Winslet — who was set to play her — visiting her home in Scotland.

Ruja targeted the vulnerable, in under-developed countries, people with very little, and she absolutely wiped them out Jennifer McAdam

Though the movie project is now on hold, the podcast has led to whistle-blowers contacting her with leads and reported sightings of Ignatova, all of which she passes on to the FBI.

The last ten years have taken a huge toll on Jennifer, who already suffered from ME, a condition which can be worsened by stress.

In one small breakthrough, this month the US Department of Justice announced that $40million, seized from Ignatova and British OneCoin co-founder Sebastian Greenwood, would be used to pay compensation to victims worldwide.



Jennifer said: “I’m delighted for the victims because it is one small glimmer of hope. It wasn’t rich people.

“Ruja targeted the vulnerable, in under-developed countries, people with very little, and she absolutely wiped them out.

“I’ve supported thousands of victims worldwide, people who are absolutely devastated, people who are suicidal. Some have died by suicide.

“For every victim I’ve spoken to who introduced family or friends, the guilt is immense. I don’t think it will ever leave me.”

News.title: Golders Green ‘terror attack’ is a punch to the gut – I’m sick of MPs hand-wringing while us Jews are targeted
News.content:
GOLDERS Green was once as familiar to me as the back of my hand.

After school was spent flirting with boys outside the tube station.





Thursday nights were at Carmelli’s, where we’d eat the bakery’s famous bagels and catch up with friends.

It is the heart of Jewish London and that’s why this latest attack, following the ambulances and the memorial wall, all in the same district, feels like a punch to the gut.

As much as our Home Secretary asserts she will “strain every sinew” to end this hatred, we all know that’s not true.

If the terrorist attack on Manchester’s Heaton Park didn’t lead to any change, if the arson attacks caused only more words, why will this be different?



I’m sick of politicians’ hand-wringing while my community is attacked.

British Jews, who have lived peacefully on these islands for hundreds of years, are moving to Israel — a literal warzone — in record numbers as they know this government will not keep us safe.



And I look around at the other parties and I see fellow hand-wringers.

We know more could be done. We saw the Government move at superspeed with the Southport riots.

Suddenly, the CPS could spot racist hate speech and the threat of arrest quickly turned the tide.



Why can’t they do it for us?

I wonder how many dead or violently attacked Jews it will take for them to do more than straining sinews to actually work out how to protect us.

News.title: Zack Polanski sparks fury after saying Jewish ‘unsafety’ may be perception amid wave of antisemitic attacks
News.content:
GREEN Party leader Zack Polanski has come under fire over remarks about the British Jewish community’s “perception of unsafety”.

Justice Minister Sarah Sackman said she only had to “turn on the news” after yesterday’s Golders Green attack to “understand the actual threat that Jews face”.





Mr Polanski, who is Jewish, was previously asked about the rise in antisemitic attacks in the wake of the arson on four Jewish ambulances in North London last month.

He said: “There’s a conversation to be had about whether it’s a perception of unsafety or it’s actual unsafety”.

Ms Sackman said: “There have been Jews stabbed in my constituency for no other reason than they are Jewish.

“And if you want to understand how racism and terror works, it’s designed to strike fear into people, not just about what’s actually happening, but what may happen.



“I hope that across the political divide, people wake up and understand that, once again, an attack on Britain’s Jews is an attack on British values.”

Mr Polanski described the latest attacks as “horrendous”.



He added: “Thinking of the victims, their families and everyone who will once again be shaken by this attack.

“Thank you to all of those involved with the emergency response.”

News.title: Charles’ hilarious US speech showed the virtue-signalling cretins he’s EXACTLY what we need to fix Special Relationship
News.content:
WELL don’t they look stupid now?

All those virtue-signalling cretins who called for the King to scrap his visit to the US this week, because, well . . . Donald Trump.



I’m looking at Ed Davey, Zack Polanski, John McDonnell, Emily Thornberry, the usual suspects struck down by Trump Derangement Syndrome.

The unpredictable Don would “embarrass” Charles, it would be a “humiliation” they sneered.

They didn’t think our monarch should be anywhere near the US President as he waged war in Iran and trampled on the Special Relationship like the doormat at his preposterous Mar-a-Lago.



Well, as I said on these pages before, this is exactly why His Maj should be jetting across the pond.

There is no emergency diplomatic fix like the royal first aid kit.

And so it came to pass. Tuesday night’s two speeches by our skilful sovereign were a masterclass in international relations. Proof, American-sized, that our King retains the vital soft-power clout of his late mother, who, in 1991, stood in the exact spot where he dazzled Congress.

And by jove, Mr Speaker, Charles, like the 1814 White House he cleverly alluded to in his evening dinner toast, was on fire.

Congress is used to hearing great speeches from foreign dignitaries — from Churchill to Mandela to Zelensky — but they are not used to hearing them from British monarchs.



Only Charles and his “mama” have been given, what the King described as “the great honour” of addressing America’s 237-year old chamber of debate. And we are all not used to hearing our frequently cranky (let’s be honest) King be so funny.

His half-hour, pitch-perfect performance in front of a “chock-full” house (it has 541 members) contained many quips that had his audience laughing and on their feet.

The assembled throng jumped up no less than 12 times to punctuate the King’s words with a standing ovation.

Zingers like this one: “250 years ago . . . or, as we say in Britain, Just the other day.”

A well-written (by others with his input) gag that spoke perfectly to an audience who cannot fathom that many Brits live in houses built more than a century ago.



Yet good script or not, effective comedy is all about the delivery.

The graveyard of public figures who have died on stage after delivering a badly timed gag has very little room left. Fortunately, charming Charles’s timing was perfect. An Edinburgh one-man show surely beckons.

We’ll call it Whose Line of Succession is it Anyway?

But the King is not in town to pitch for the Oscar for Best Comedy Performance. He is there to repair a relationship that at times recently has seemed busted beyond repair.

Bonhomie and banter

So his speeches contained more serious and, at times, coded messages, like the importance of maintaining Nato and defending Ukraine, two subjects that seem to endlessly irritate Trump.



They landed without fuss. If the President was rattled, he, uncharacteristically, did not show it.

Has it changed his view? We shall have to wait and see.

For now it is all bonhomie and banter.

Yet while giddy Trump may be all sweetness and light as he joshes with his revered guest, there is no escaping the fact he has fomented an unhelpful disdain for our nation.

Some of the blame for this, of course, must be laid at the door of our calamitous PM, who has demonstrated he would fail a GCSE in US diplomacy.



Sir Keir Starmer, like his colleagues Thornberry and McDonnell, is suffering from a touch of the old TDS and has let it cloud his judgment.

Would Trump have been so abrasive about the islands that produced his mother had Starmer taken a more pragmatic approach to our old friend across the pond?

I think we know the answer.

So it has been left to the King to rise above the current fray and remind our American friends that our relationship is a deep-rooted one that has stood the test of time.

A union able to withstand the potshots from an increasingly irascible, by any metric, 47th president and his blinkered acolytes.



Britain should be thankful that “in times of great uncertainty” we have a level-headed, expert envoy who can clear up the mess our elected leader has created.

BIBLE IS OFF BRAND

MY sides are still in agony after Piers Morgan’s silent takedown of Russell Brand on his Uncensored show.

The excitable evangelist’s failure to find the Bible passages he claimed had helped him through his last court appearance was priceless, as were the millions of memes it generated.

But the humiliation didn’t end there.



“Christian” Brand took his lack of self-awareness to new heights by tweeting Piers the following day to say he had finally found the passage that had so embarrassingly escaped him. Eek!

Only a deluded imbecile like him could think that his interviewer had ever cared what passage it was.

Piers, like the rest of us, had a hunch you were a fraud.

You just went and confirmed it.

A LORRY carrying 20 TONNES of Prosecco crashed this week on the M4, drenching the carriageway with those delicious Italian bubbles (and shattered glass).



That equates to 1,500 bottles, which will make some dent in the supply for anyone in the Berkshire area.

Bang goes this weekend’s bottomless brunch.

CHIPS AHOY FEEL for the bloke saddled with 540 bags of potatoes he can’t shift after a chip shop cancelled its order. He’s now got a warehouse full of 12 tonnes of unwanted spuds. Or to put that in terms of the generous servings they dish out at my local chippie . . . two large portions. CHIPS are “crispier, saltier and more delicious” when nabbed off someone else, according to an important study this week. Apparently it’s all to do with the added rush of enjoyment experienced by the guilt of what we’re doing. Finally, we have an answer to why seagulls never buy their own.

DAVID IS THE MAKER OF HIS OWN DOWNFALL

DING DING, it’s round one of the Rumble In The Jungle 2026.

In the blue corner it’s the undisputed heavyweight misogynist David “The Troublemaker” Haye.



And in the red corner tonight it’s the poor saps at ITV who had the temerity to offer this former cruiserweight champ a chance to reboot his career.

Haye is so miffed at his portrayal on I’m A Celeb, he’s “instructed lawyers” and plans to sue ITV for £10million.

Whether this ever makes it to court though… feels unlikely.

Because the simple truth here is that David Haye is the architect of his own negative press.

As we have seen with many boxers over the years, too many blows to the head have rendered him a hotheaded, thin-skinned, vainglorious moron who cannot comprehend that the world sees him for what he is.



I hope ITV KO’s his vexatious claim.

LEAVE PUTIN TO MEG

I WAS reading a report today about the war in Ukraine, and the gist of it seemed to be Russia’s barbarous campaign was still going on.

Which cannot possibly be right because just the other day, Prince Harry told Vladimir Putin to stop.

If Mad Vlad won’t listen to him, who will he listen to?



Well maybe there is someone. Indeed, Harry should have got his wife to order the Russian maniac to stand down.

After all, as the hen-pecked Prince famously barked at his flunkeys: “What Meghan wants, Meghan gets.”

MUCH mocking from Reform UK haters that their fuel protest in London on Monday looked like the car park at Sainsbury’s at 6pm on a Sunday.

But the lack of attendance by angry motorists rather proves their point.

As smallbusiness owner Keith Steers said, to get to the protest he had to fork out £18 for the congestion charge, a £12.50 Ulez fee then however much of the £1.50-odd-a-litre fuel he used getting to and from Leighton Buzzard. So north of £50!



I’m amazed they had anyone there at all.

News.title: Moment 30ft ‘shark’ is spotted off UK coast as stunned family watch in horror
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a monster shark, believed to be more than 30ft long, is spotted off the British Isles.

Footage shows the giant sea creature at the surface, thrashing its tail in dramatic scenes and sending jaws dropping among stunned onlookers.





Another clip showed its dorsal fin slicing through the water in classic Jaws style, sparking fears of a deadly predator.

But despite its terrifying appearance, the huge fish turned out to be a harmless basking shark, as reported by creatorzine.com.

The beast was spotted alongside others off Aranmore Island in County Donegal.

Skipper John Paul Baska of Northwest Charters had a family on board his boat when the giant emerged.

He said: “It was big, maybe 35-feet-long.

“I have seen bigger ones.



“But the family of five who were on the charter were impressed.

“There was plenty of plankton for the sharks to feed on.

“And great fishing too.”



The basking shark is the second-largest fish in the world, beaten only by the whale shark.

It is one of just three plankton-eating sharks, alongside the whale shark and the rare megamouth shark.

These giants can be found swimming alone or in small groups.

Despite their size and fearsome look, they pose no danger to humans.

Grey-brown adults grow to an average of 20-26ft and weigh five tons but they can be much bigger.

The largest accurately measured was caught in Canada in 1851 and weighed 16 tons.



It was 40.3ft (12.27m) long.

Specimens longer than 33ft are rarely seen these days because over-fishing has reduced their numbers.

Basking sharks have enormous mouths more than three feet wide, with jaws that stretch open as they feed in shallow waters close to shore.

Their babies are huge as well. They are born, measuring five or six feet long, after a gestation thought to last from one to three years.

They are a protected red list species, considered vulnerable worldwide and endangered in the North East Atlantic.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Basking sharks migrate here every summer and are found all round the British Isles from the English Channel to the far north of Scotland.

They are mostly solitary but schools have been seen gathering in the Hebrides.

News.title: Golders Green security organisation pledge to increase patrols
News.content:
Golders Green security organisation pledge to increase patrols

Shomrim organisations operate in Jewish communities around the world with the north-west London branch being established in 2008 and now operating community safety patrols six nights a week, resting only for Shabbat and High Holidays

View 5 Images Shomrim patrol volunteer Yonathan Elkouby helped stop the suspect

The Golders Green suspect was arrested by police with help from a hero patrol officer from the Jewish community safety group Shomrim.

‌



Volunteer Yonathan Elkouby joined two Metropolitan police officers in wrestling the alleged knifeman to the ground after two people were stabbed outside a synagogue on Wednesday.

‌



He has told how he locked eyes with the man, saying: "I managed to block him off, and with the police, we managed to put him down. "At one point, he made eye contact with me, and came at me."

‌



Shomrim, Hebrew for "watchers" or "guards", are often compared to a private police force due their uniforms, which can include stab-proof vests and yellow caps. They carry out regular patrols in parts of north and east London and operate a 999-style 24-hour emergency line.

But, although they say they work in conjunction with the Met Police, they have no legal powers and are a registered charity, which is funded entirely privately, with no government help. They are a Jewish run group, but can be called for help by any member of the community, regardless of their religion.

View 5 Images Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis spoke with Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Shomrim organisations operate in Jewish communities around the world. The Shomrim NW London branch was established in 2008 following a large spate of burglaries and crime in the area.

It now operates community safety patrols six nights a week, resting only for Shabbat and High Holidays, with volunteers completing training from the Metropolitan Police Counter Terrorism Command.

It says its organisation is staffed by unpaid male and female volunteers who give their time to patrol the local neighbourhood, "facilitating the arrest and prosecution of hundreds of criminals every year".

‌



Shomrim officer Ben Grossnass , 40, has been called out to a number of serious reports of attacks in recent months, including the blowing up of four private Jewish ambulances close to the scene of today's attack.

He believes Shomrim, who specialise in dealing with hate crimes, child safeguarding and missing people, is needed more than ever. Ben said: "There is a lot of hate in society and antisemitism. We're currently really stretched with the ongoing uptake of antisemitism, but we are here for the safety of the community.

View 5 Images Police cars near the scene (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

‌



"There are ways the Government can crack down on this and it is time they did that. We've been around as a local organisation assisting the police with different investigations and situations that take place on our streets in London for 17 years.

"Currently and never have we been supported financially by the government. We are extremely stretched, we are a good resource for them, especially for our local community. It's time they put their hand in their pocket and assisted us the way we need it."

Ben, who describes his work helping keep people safe as "his passion", added: "People have got to really speak up and make sure they're heard and the government should be standing shoulder to shoulder with our community ensuring safety."

‌



The dad-of-four admits he is fearful for his children in Britain. Asked if he believes they have a safe future, he admitted: "I'm not sure of that. No one's sure of anything, but we will be more certain if the government are there to assist us."

View 5 Images A Shomrim patrol officer speaking to a community member (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Writing on Shomrim North West's official X account, a spokesperson said: "The incident has now been declared a terrorist attack by @TerrorismPolice. This marks the second terrorist incident targeting the Jewish community in the UK within seven months.

‌



"In addition to the numerous arson attacks against the Jewish community in NW London in recent weeks. Our brave @ShomrimLondon colleagues acted swiftly, together with @metpoliceuk, helping detain the suspect and ensure a swift arrest. Shomrim, London North and East will be increasing patrols and security, working closely with police and partners. If you see something, say something. Please report anything suspicious."

Another message added: "Following today’s terror attack and the recent incidents in NW London, the work of Shomrim NW London is more vital than ever. Operating 24/7, we remain dedicated to protecting and supporting the community, relying heavily on the generosity of the public. Please consider supporting our essential work."

Shomrim's website says: "In the majority of cases where Shomrim have helped to secure a conviction, the victim of the crime was not Jewish. Members of the local Jewish community, especially for those whom Yiddish or Hebrew is their first language, often feel more comfortable calling Shomrim, than contacting the police. However, Shomrim’s Emergency Line is available to everyone, and each year, hundreds of people call to benefit from Shomrim’s fast response times and extensive knowledge of the local area."

‌



"One of Shomrim’s most important duties is helping victims of hate crimes, and assisting them through the process of bringing the perpetrators to justice. We are proud to say that last year we facilitated 22 arrests following anti-Semitic incidents, of which 11 resulted in prosecutions. Victims of antisemitic crimes who receive support from Shomrim are much more likely to see the perpetrators brought to justice than the national average."

View 5 Images Members of the Jewish community have been left concerned by the latest attack, which follows a spate of arsons in the area (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Outlining the training it's volunteers receive, the website says: "All Shomrim volunteers go through an extensive screening and training process to ensure that they can cope with the pressure and act exclusively within the law. Every Shomrim volunteer receives training in counter-terrorism and first aid, as well as training on crime prevention by the Metropolitan police.

‌



"All Shomrim volunteers are DBS checked. While on patrol, they wear stab-proof vests and carry an ID card, a two-way radio, and a first aid kit. Because of their unparalleled knowledge of the local area, our volunteers are able to gather evidence that would otherwise be unavailable to the police, as well as prevent crimes before they happen.

"While on patrol, Shomrim volunteers protect all members of the community, regardless of ethnicity or religion, creating an environment where local residents of diverse backgrounds know that Shomrim’s neighbourhood patrols can be relied on to act with professionalism and compassion."

It adds: "Shomrim proactively patrol and operate primarily, but not exclusively in the areas of Golders Green, Childs Hill, Hendon, Finchley and Temple Fortune with nightly hi-vis patrolling vehicles that serve as a deterrent for criminals who may want to engage in criminal activity. Shomrim’s 24hr emergency response team are dispatched daily to incidents reported to our emergency number. Volunteers communicate through a pan London two way radio system via a central controller.

Article continues below

"Shomrim volunteers patrolling by foot and in vehicles serve and act as an extension to the Metropolitan Police Service eyes and ears by report suspicious incidents and crimes within the community to the Police. When Shomrim is dispatched to a scene of a crime, our volunteers then bridge the time gap between when Police are called and when Police attend.

"This enables Shomrim to follow suspects and preserve evidence until the arrival of Police. The visible patrol vehicle serves as a deterrent for criminals who may wish to operate in the area. Shomrim has the capability to deal with various scenarios including the locating of missing persons. Protocols are in place for full scale searches across the capital. Shomrim work very closely with other agencies and voluntary sector organisations."

News.title: Body of missing boy, 19, found in River Tees as heartbroken family pay tribute
News.content:
Body of missing boy, 19, found in River Tees as heartbroken family pay tribute

Joseph Porch had been missing since Wednesday, April 22, and was last seen on CCTV in the Scotswood House area, in Thornaby, near the River Tees in Stockton

View 2 Images The body of Joseph Porch has been found (Image: North News & Pictures Ltd northnews.co.uk)

A body has been pulled from a river in the search for a missing teenager.

‌



Joseph Porch, 19, had been missing since Wednesday, April 22, and was last seen on CCTV in the Scotswood House area of Stockton-on-Tees, in Thornaby, near the River Tees.

‌



Cleveland Police has now confirmed that during the search his body was found in the River Tees on Wednesday morning, April 29. Formal identification has now been carried out.

‌



View 2 Images Joseph had been missing for a week (Image: Cleveland Police)

Iran war live: Trump shares AI picture of himself with gun in new threat to Tehran READ MORE :

His parents said in a statement how they were "devasted" at the loss of their "beautiful son" while thanking the rescue services for their efforts to find Joseph.

"We are devastated at the loss of our beautiful son. We will forever love him and be proud of him," they said. “Special thanks to Cleveland Police, Northumbria Police Diving Unit, Cleveland Fire and Rescue Service and Tees River Rescue in their devoted efforts to locate him.

‌



"We'd like to thank our family and friends for their support and would now ask for some time for our family to take in this tragedy and remember our son at this difficult time."

Cleveland Police said that the death is not being treated as suspicion and a file is being prepared for a coroner.

The force said: "Sadly, during the search for missing 19-year-old Joseph Porch (also known as Joey), his body was located this morning (Wednesday 29th April) in the River Tees in Stockton.

Article continues below

"Formal identification has been carried out this afternoon. Our thoughts remain with Joseph’s family and friends at this extremely difficult time. The death is not being treated as suspicious, and a file will be prepared for the Coroner."

Many people have taken to social media to express their sadness at the news. One person wrote on Facebook: "Thoughts and Prayers to the family, may he R.I.P." Another comment read: "So so sad my heartfelt condolences to family and friends, fly high forever young beautiful boy."

And a further person wrote: "Heartbreaking sending our Condolences to his family/ friends another young life gone far to soon Rip young man."

News.title: Trump draws King into Iran war again saying he 'would have probably helped'
News.content:
Trump draws King into Iran war again saying he 'would have probably helped'

As Charles continues his US state visit, the president has proclaimed that Charles “would have helped” the US with their offensive in the Middle East

View 3 Images Trump has made a series of bold statements about the King and his stance on the war in the Middle East (Image: Getty)

President Trump has boldly proclaimed that King Charles “would have probably helped” the United States with their offensive against Iran, once again drawing the monarch into the war in the Middle East.

‌



Charles and Camilla departed Washington DC earlier today to continue their state visit on the East Coast, just hours after his rousing address to Congress in which the King called for peace and togetherness during turbulent times in global politics.

‌



As Their Majesties left the US capital and headed to New York, Trump took questions in the Oval Office and was asked how his meeting with the King went.

‌



View 3 Images Trump has dragged Charles, once again, into the war in Iran (Image: Ian Vogler/Daily Mirror/PA Wire)

Trump was asked about Charles’ address to Congress, in which the monarch praised the work of NATO and made a few subtle digs at the US president and his unpredictable administration.

In the Oval Office, Trump said he was "very disappointed" in NATO after the US "asked them to do some things about Ukraine and Iran". He continued: "The King is fantastic. We spent a lot of time together. We talked a lot. We talked about this also. He loves his country, and he's a great King. And he's a great friend. I think if he were doing that, if that were up to him, he would have probably helped us with Iran."

‌



Elsewhere during the questioning in the Oval Office, Trump was asked about his relationship with Keir Starmer, to which Trump said his good relationship with the King after their successful trip to Washington could help his relationship with the UK prime minister.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump’s comments come just hours after he took to Truth Social, where he posted an image of himself holding a gun with destruction in the background, with the words: "No More Mr Nice Guy". The caption read: "Iran can’t get their act together. They don’t know how to sign a nonnuclear deal. They better get smart soon! President DJT."

‌



During the state dinner Trump insisted the King agrees with him that Iran should never be allowed nuclear weapons. As head of state, the King is above party politics and remains neutral but Trump’s comments are likely to cause some embarrassment to royal aides that his views have been made public.

A Buckingham Palace spokesperson said: “The King is naturally mindful of his Government’s long-standing and well-known position on the prevention of nuclear proliferation.”

View 3 Images President Trump and King Charles during the ceremonial welcome at the White House (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



After leaving Washington DC this morning, Charles and Camilla honoured the lives of the victims and survivors of the 9/11 terror attacks in New York City. On the third day of their US tour, the royal couple were joined by former New York mayor Michael Bloomberg as they laid a wreath on the 9/11 Memorial.

Written on a handwritten note, in the King’s distinctive black script, placed alongside the flowers, the monarch wrote: “We honour the memory for those who so tragically lost their lives on 11th September 2001. We stand in enduring solidarity with the American people and in the face of their profound loss. Charles R Camilla.”

News.title: Jet2 passenger 'violent' on flight calmed down by boy, 8, as plane narrowly avoids diversion
News.content:
Jet2 passenger 'violent' on flight calmed down by boy, 8, as plane narrowly avoids diversion

Dad James Rose, 42, and his eight-year-old son Phoenix were praised for calming a disruptive passenger on a Jet2 flight to Manchester – but James insists his son deserves all the credit

View 3 Images Phoenix Rose has been praised for calming a disruptive passenger (Image: Manchester Evening News)

A dad who prevented a Manchester-bound Jet2 flight from being diverted by calming down a disruptive passenger says his eight-year-old son is the 'real hero'.

James Rose, 42, of Salford, and his lad Phoenix intervened to pacify a troublesome traveller on a plane from Izmir, Turkey, last Friday.

Passenger John Henderson, 47, previously told the Manchester Evening News the flight was scheduled to depart at 8pm, but lifted off 50 minutes behind schedule after roughly 20 passengers were transferred from another, cancelled, service.

Mr Henderson said the trouble kicked off around 30 minutes into the flight, just after the initial drinks service. A woman, he said, was consuming her own alcohol, which was seized.

Longest non-stop flight in the world will have passengers strapped in for 22 hours READ MORE :

View 3 Images Phoenix has been hailed by his dad for calming the situation on board the Jet2 flight (Image: GordZam via Getty Images)

'She then just erupted, calling them names, being violent towards them," he said. Cabin crew, Mr Henderson said, warned the woman the aircraft would be diverted if she didn't calm down.

Another man, now identified as Mr Rose, asked if he could step in and talk to the woman. The disruptive passenger was relocated to sit next to him. Mr Rose remained with the woman and kept her composed, Mr Henderson said.

"He listened to her, he talked to her, he was completely in control of the whole situation," he said. "The stewardesses couldn't thank him enough. They kept on saying 'you don't know how much money you've saved Jet2 here'."

View 3 Images Pheonix Rose, who has been praised by his dad (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Mr Henderson said the man's son, now identified as young Phoenix, was an 'absolute superstar', chatting to the woman and assisting his dad. "He was getting out football cards, constantly in conversation with her," he told the Manchester Evening News.

Mr Rose said he was astonished by the reaction to the story, but insisted the praise must go entirely to his son. He and Phoenix were travelling home after abandoning their holiday due to a family emergency.

"I'm not the hero," Mr Rose said. "It was me lad. The way he handled the situation, he calmed her down. She was swearing and calling them every name under the sun."

"One of the stewardesses said 'that's it, we're gonna call the pilot and get this plane diverted'. I said 'can you give me 30 seconds'. I asked if we could get her sat next to me."

"We put her in the middle between me and my lad and that's when my lad took over. He was absolutely fantastic, he took over. He was saying to her 'don't shout, don't swear... what do your kids do?'."

"My lad stuck to her like glue," James said. "Every time she tried to go off he would tap her and say 'come on, talk to me'. It was just magnificent to see."

Mr Rose added: "As soon as that plane touched down, relief kicked in. We got in a taxi and went home and never thought nothing of it. When I've seen the comments, I was shocked with the response. People are saying really nice things."

Phoenix, his dad said, just hopes the woman is okay. "He's been asking how the lady is," Mr Rose said. "He's very thoughtful and said 'I hope she gets the help and care she needs'."

"Even last night when I was going to bed I had a tear in my eye because I don't actually think I would've been able to do it myself. I think the overriding factor was Phoenix. If anyone is a hero, it's him."

Article continues below

Reflecting on the experience, Mr Rose said: "My mum always taught me that you help people and it's nice to be nice. If we could help one person, fantastic." Greater Manchester Police confirmed officers attended the scene, though no crimes were reported.

News.title: Package holiday price hikes warning as cost can go up after you've booked
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Package holiday price hikes warning as cost can go up after you've booked

Looking to go on holiday this summer? Experts predicting holiday havoc thanks to war in the Middle East, warn that holiday prices can rise - after you’ve booked.

View 4 Images Orange beach also known as Mega Portokali is one of the most beautiful beaches of Sithonia peninsula - a greek paradise. But this summer a trip there could be pricey... (Image: Getty Images)

The devil is in the detail, according to an investigation by the Tonight programme, which reveals that small print in package holiday deals means firms can increase prices after you thought the deal was done. Jo Rhodes, travel expert with consumer group, Which? says: “The package holiday providers can ask for more money even after you've booked. Up to 8% of what you’ve paid. Anything over that and you have a right to cancel for a full refund.”

‌



According to the Association of British Travel Agencies (ABTA) and Which? the surcharge is allowed for specific cost increases, including fuel, taxes or exchange rates, provided it’s in the terms and conditions. The war with Iran also means popular holiday hotspots like Dubai, Turkey and Cyprus are facing an uncertain summer.

‌



The UK government is advising against travel to within 10km of the Turkish border with Syria, “due to fighting and a heightened risk of terrorism”. And, after a drone struck RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus in March, travel company SPL villas saw an 80% drop in searches for holidays there.

‌



View 4 Images Airline Lufthansa has cancelled 20,000 flights this summer to save on jet fuel. (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Airline Lufthansa has cancelled 20,000 flights this summer to save on jet fuel. Aviation analyst John Grant says: “It’s unprecedented. We've got this domino effect of disruption.” Russian airspace is closed to most airlines. Ukraine is closed and there are closures in the Gulf region and Iran. Aircraft flying across the Middle East are using two narrow routes to navigate around conflict zones.

Knock-on effects include longer journey times. John says: “The bigger issue if this continues, will be the availability of jet fuel.” In the UK, airlines have called on the government to provide emergency support, because the Strait of Hormuz - a key route for jet fuel coming out of the Middle East - has been heavily disrupted by the war.”

‌



Meanwhile, knowing your rights is essential for travellers. Jo Rhodes explains: “I'd really advise people to consider a package holiday. If anything goes wrong, you're protected by the package travel regulations. If you do want to book things separately, it's a really good idea to fly with a UK or EU airline because, again, you get more protection.”

Travel insurance is essential, but people must read the small print. Jo says: “Only a third of policies actually cover war or conflict.” Travellers should also be aware of the “known event clause.” Jo says: “If you know about a situation before you travel, this could make you less entitled to claim later.”

View 4 Images Travelling abroad this summer could be an expensive affair (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Travelling to a destination against government advice could also impact your cover. UK staycations have enjoyed a surge in interest because of global unrest. One traveller, Andrew Holland, tells Tonight a UK holiday makes perfect sense.

Beverley holiday park in Devon has seen a surge in bookings. But director Claire Flower still fears increased bills, rates and wages, combined with a possible tourist tax - currently being considered for England and already in place in Scotland and Wales - could make UK tourism tricky. Claire says of a potential tourist tax: “Customers are going to find it difficult to pay that little bit more.”

At Lincombe Hall hotel and spa in Torquay, Devon, manager Peter Watkins told Tonight that their £60,000 annual energy bill will soon soar and force him to increase prices on spa days, while trying to keep overnight stays the same.

‌



He says: “There's a limit to what people can pay. We'd rather get people in and let them enjoy themselves than price ourselves out of the market, but we've got to remain profitable.” The new system designed to track every non-EU traveller - including those from the UK - entering the 29 European countries comprising the ‘Schengen’ area is another added hassle.

View 4 Images Paul Charles on ITV's Tonight programme (Image: Supplied)

British travellers have to stop, register their details and submit biometric data the first time they enter the Schengen area. Reportedly taking far longer than expected, some passengers have missed flights and airports and airlines warn the system could struggle to cope during peak months.

‌



The European Commission told Tonight: “Europe now has the most modern IT Border System in the world. The core purpose is to make our borders more secure and protect EU citizens."

*Tonight- Holiday Havoc: Where Should You Go? On at 7:30pm, Thursday, ITV and ITVX

Expert travel tips

-Reduction in demand for holidays in the Eastern Mediterranean, because of global unrest, means there are cheap deals. Luke Fitzpatrick, from Perfect Getaways in Liverpool, says: “We have seen Turkey and Cyprus coming up with really good prices from around £249 per person [for a week].”

Article continues below

-Travel expert Chelsea Dickinson advises picking places that are cheap when you get there, saying: “A place for me that ticks all those boxes, that has fantastic links from all over the UK is Poland. Other places could be Bulgaria, Albania. In central and Eastern Europe, there are so many gems where your money could go a lot further.”

-Consider traveling outside the school summer holidays. Tonight compared one week all-inclusive trips to Greece and Spain across four major operators and found families could save an average of £689 in Greece and £381 in Spain, by going a week before school holidays start.

News.title: Cobra kills tourist in Egypt holiday hotspot after 'slithering up trousers'
News.content:
Cobra kills tourist in Egypt holiday hotspot after 'slithering up trousers'

A 57-year-old German man has tragically died at a snake charming show at a luxury beach resort in Egypt after he was bitten by a highly-venomous cobra

View Image A German tourist was bitten by a snake (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A tourist has died after a snake crawled up his pants and bit him as he watched a show on a family holiday in Egypt.

‌



The 57-year-old German was watching the snake-charming event at a hotel in Hurghada, a luxury beach resort on the Red Sea, in early April when the incident happened.

‌



Two snakes, reported to be cobras, were draped around the upper-bodies of the audience who had come to see the show.

‌



It is understood that the victim then allowed a snake to crawl up his trousers which was when he was bitten.

Met Office forecasts 26C as UK hotter than Zante – maps reveal exactly where READ MORE :

Police in Bavaria said: "During the snake charmer’s performance, one of the snakes crawled into the trousers of a 57-year-old man, resulting in a bite to the German tourist’s leg.”

The victim showed "clear signs of poisoning" and had to be resuscitated before being taken to hospital, but he later died, said a statement from German police.

‌



The man, who was not named in the statement, came from the Unterallgaeu district in Bavaria and was on holiday with two family members.

German police and prosecutors are investigating his death and are awaiting the results of a toxicology test.

The police statement added: "The investigation into the circumstances of the death is being conducted by the Memmingen Criminal Police Inspectorate under the direction of the Memmingen Public Prosecutor's Office. The results of a toxicological examination are still pending.

Article continues below

It appears as though it is normal for performers at the snake charming shows to allow the reptiles to crawl over guests and that they are place around their necks.

Cobras are known for being highly venomous as most possess neurotoxic venom, which attacks the central nervous system and can lead to rapid paralysis and respiratory failure. Without intervention, such as antivenom or mechanical ventilation, a bite from a large species like the King Cobra can be fatal in as little as 30 minutes.

Snake charming remains very controversial due to the danger but also the practice has been criticised by animal rights organisations which have long lobbied against them for being cruel and often used as a tourist trap in parts of the world.

News.title: Professor Green 'nearly died' during substance abuse as he issues major warning
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Professor Green 'nearly died' during substance abuse as he issues major warning

Rapper, presenter and podcadter Professor Green - aka Stephen Manderson - is a key campaigner for men's mental health and says his life spiralled to a dark place two years ago

View 4 Images Rapper, presenter and podcaster Professor Green, aka Stephen Manderson (Image: Maja Smiejkowska)

Professor Green says he was once on a dark road that could have led to suicide, as he campaigns for men struggling with mental health issues to seek help. The multi-platinum-selling rapper, 42, real name Stephen Manderson, lost his father to suicide 18 years ago and was diagnosed with ADHD and autism at 40. He said: “Forty years of being me nearly killed me. And I don’t think it’s dissimilar to what a lot of people go through when we hit middle age.”

‌



Stephen spearheaded a study by the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy which reveals 65% of men have faced mental health issues in the past three years. But 70% of the 2,500 men surveyed will only consider therapy if they reach breaking point.

‌



Stephen’s father Peter took his own life when the star was 24, but the rapper said of his struggles: “I’ve never tried to kill myself, but through misuse of substances, to a really dangerous extent and in isolation, there was every chance of death by misadventure could have occurred.”

‌



View 4 Images Doting dad Stephen with his son, Slimane

Stephen, who co-parents his son Slimane, five, with his ex, actress Karima McAdams, hit rock bottom two years ago. He said: “I thought, ‘Am I an addict?’ I don’t think I am. It’s not something I wake up and do.’ I was always at crisis point and trying to cope. They were escape ­decisions. [The] crisis point took me to a psychiatrist two years ago, which led me to my ADHD and autism assessment. I didn’t understand any of it.

‌



“Coming out the other side and sitting with the shame of it, but realising that there was every chance that it [suicide] could have happened, I could have put my son through everything I went through and then some. I was going through stuff I couldn’t tolerate. I think that’s a huge problem with lots of men. Men generally only seek help at the point of crisis.”

Now clean and sober, Stephen, of Brockley, South East London, collaborated with Health Secretary Wes Streeting on the first men’s health strategy for England. Launched last year, it focuses on suicide prevention, and alcohol and gambling issues. As a spokesman for BACP, Stephen wants to help improve ­education around male mental health. He said therapy and being a parent have helped him resolve issues around his dad’s suicide. He said: “I was young and I didn’t understand. I’d assessed the loss of my dad from every point, but never from the point of view of a parent.”

4 View 4 Images Karima McAdams and Professor Green attend the launch of Giz & Green Pizza Pies Pop-Up at Passo on July 17, 2020 in London (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images for PASSO) 4 View 4 Images Stephen with Emile Sande in 2014 (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Stephen was married to reality star Millie Mackintosh from 2013 to 2016, and split from Karima in 2024, after a five-year engagement. He has also needed surgery in recent years for an intestinal problem. The Read All About It star released a new single, No Management, in January and is joining Example, aka Elliot Gleave, on tour in May. Stephen added: “Getting older is a luxury, there’s only one alternative."

Find out more at outside-view.co.uk

News.title: 'Families of murdered women channelled unimaginable grief into important change'
News.content:
'Families of murdered women channelled unimaginable grief into important change'

Claire Waxman, the Victims' Commissioner for England and Wales, writes for The Mirror about a change in the law to force offenders to attend their sentencing hearings in court

View 3 Images Farah, the aunt of Zara Aleena (above), told the Victims' Commissioner the offender’s absence in court felt like “a kick in the teeth” (Image: SWNS)

As the Victims and Courts Bill gains Royal Assent, it marks the culmination of years of campaigning for change by bereaved victims and families. Long-fought-for protections has just become law. More importantly, it demonstrates what becomes possible when the justice system listens to those it exists to serve.

‌



Too often, victims and families are left feeling like bystanders in proceedings that profoundly affect their lives. A criminal justice system focused on process can feel distant and unresponsive to their pain. This is felt most acutely at sentencing, when offenders are able to choose not to attend hearings - one of the very few moments when victims and families are finally given a voice.

‌



The families of Sabina Nessa, Zara Aleena and Jan Mustafa channelled unimaginable grief into determined, purposeful campaigning to ensure this harm was properly recognised. Jebina Nessa, Sabina’s sister, was among the first to bring national attention to the impact of offenders refusing to attend sentencing. Cheryl Korbel campaigned for change following the murder of her daughter Olivia, adding her voice to growing calls for action on offenders’ non-attendance at sentencing.

‌



Ayse, whose cousin Jan Mustafa was murdered in 2018, described standing alone in court, reading words forged in grief “to no one”. Farah, the aunt of Zara Aleena, told me the offender’s absence felt like “a kick in the teeth”.

Vile criminals who try to dodge justice will face fresh punishment under new Labour law READ MORE :

View 3 Images Farah Naz, Ayse Hussein, Keir Starmer, Jebina Islam and Claire Waxman in July last year

Hearing directly from these families about the additional harm caused by non-attendance strengthened my determination to work alongside them and press for change.

‌



The sentencing hearing is one of the very few moments in the justice process where victims and families are given a voice. When an offender wilfully refuses to attend, it compounds trauma and strips that moment of accountability. These families were clear: their calls for change were not about retribution. They were about recognition, dignity and the basic expectation that those who cause the most serious harm should face the consequences of their actions.

Because they spoke out – and because their lived experience was listened to – the law is now changing. In July of last year, I was privileged to accompany these inspiring individuals to Number 10 to meet the Prime Minister and discuss their tireless work that helped change the law – ensuring offenders are compelled to attend sentencing.

Under the Victims and Courts Act, courts will have powers to compel attendance at sentencing hearings, with consequences for those who continue to refuse, including additional time added to their sentence and the loss of privileges. Even small extensions to a sentence matter deeply to families because they represent acknowledgement that further harm was caused.

‌



This reform did not appear overnight. It exists because victims and bereaved families refused to accept being sidelined, and instead spent years campaigning with determination, dignity and courage to ensure their experiences shaped the law.

View 3 Images Claire Waxman said the changes to the law were “the culmination of years of campaigning for change by bereaved victims and families” (Image: Internet Unknown)

The same is true of reforms to the Unduly Lenient Sentencing (ULS) scheme. Under the new reforms, victims and bereaved families will be given significantly more time to challenge sentences they believe do not reflect the seriousness of the crime.

‌



Following the murder of her son Josh, Tracey Hanson campaigned tirelessly to expose the lack of parity between the rights of victims and offenders within the scheme. While offenders are informed of their appeal rights and can apply outside the 28-day limit in exceptional circumstances, many victims are never told the scheme exists and are bound by a rigid deadline.

Despite raising concerns about the sentence, Tracey was not informed of the scheme and only became aware of it on the final day of the 28-day window. Although she submitted her application immediately, it was rejected as out of time. Her determination helped bring national attention to systemic gaps that left victims feeling powerless and unheard. Katie Brett has also spoken out powerfully following the murder of her sister Sasha, supporting calls for the scheme to be extended so families are not left without meaningful routes to challenge a sentence.

Tracey called for two clear changes: for the rigid 28-day time limit to be extended in exceptional circumstances, and for responsibility for informing victims and bereaved families about the scheme to sit clearly with a single, accountable agency.

‌



Under the new reforms, victims and bereaved families will now have up to six months to ask for a sentence to be reconsidered, where it is in the interests of justice to do so. The government will also introduce a legal duty in the Victims’ Code to notify victims of the existence of the ULS scheme, ensuring families are informed of their right to challenge a sentence and how to do so.

Both reforms go to the heart of why the role of Victims’ Commissioner exists. The purpose of my role is to ensure that the lived experience of victims is used to improve legislation, policy and practice. As someone who has lived with the impact of stalking for over two decades, I know personally how easily victims can be marginalised by systems that prioritise process over people.

The Bill also strengthens my powers as Victims’ Commissioner, enabling greater scrutiny of how agencies respond to victims and how commitments made on paper translate into practice. That oversight matters. Without proper resourcing, training and cultural change across the justice system, even the most well-intentioned reforms risk falling short.

Article continues below

As we approach Royal Assent, this moment is about recognition - recognising the courage and persistence of campaigners who refused to be silenced. But it is also a reminder that legislation alone is never enough. The true test of these reforms will be whether they are implemented effectively, consistently and with the seriousness they deserve.

The Victims and Courts Bill shows what is possible when lived experience is taken seriously. Now, government and criminal justice agencies must deliver on what has been promised.

Atletico Madrid host Arsenal in the first leg of their Champions League semi-finals, with both teams still in pursuit of a maiden trophy in Europe’s top tier.

Donald Trump has claimed that King Charles “probably would have helped us” in Iran in another attack on prime minister Sir Keir Starmer and Nato.

As the King and Queen were in New York during their four-day state visit, the US president said the monarch was a “phenomenal representative for his country” and suggested he would have differed in his approach to the conflict from the prime minister.

He said: “The King loves his country, and he's a great king, and he's a great friend of mine. And I think if that it were up to him, he would have probably helped us with Iran.”

open image in gallery Former New York mayor Michael Bloomberg, the King and Queen Camilla attended a ceremony at the National September 11 Memorial ( Getty )

Asked by reporters whether the King’s speech that referred to the need for a strong Nato alliance had changed his mind, Mr Trump said he was very disappointed in Nato after the US “asked them to do some things about Ukraine and Iran”.

Praising the King as “fantastic”, he added: “He would have done– he would have followed the suggestions we made with respect to Ukraine, because, you know, we have some disagreements on Ukraine and not having to do with Nato so much as European countries.”

His remarks were another veiled dig at the prime minister, whom he has previously dismissed as “not Winston Churchill”.

Mr Trump said the King would see him before he left for home. “I think he's a phenomenal representative for his country,” he said.

“I think the people in the United Kingdom should be proud.

“I loved his speech yesterday. I watched it. I loved the speech last night. I don't know about my speech. I thought my speech was okay, too, but I thought he was I think he's an unbelievable King, and, by the way, an unbelievable queen. They are a great couple.”

open image in gallery Mr Trump, who touched the King on the knee, praised the royals – in contrast with his attitude to Sir Keir Starmer ( Getty )

The US president has repeatedly condemned Nato for what he sees as relying too much on the US for funding and successfully pressured allies to increase their defence spending.

He has also attacked other allies, including the UK, for not supporting the US-Israeli war on Iran, and has more than once threatened to pull America out of the Nato defensive alliance.

Mr Trump last year demanded that all Nato nations stop buying Russian oil and energy immediately. Although most halted or reduced the amounts they were buying, some countries, such as Hungary, remained a big customer for Moscow’s gas industry.

In his efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, the president has repeatedly pressurised Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky into ceding land to Moscow. Under plans he drew up last year, Kyiv would also have had to give up on its ambition of joining Nato.

In contrast with his attacks on Nato, the EU and other allies, Mr Trump has been unwavering in his flattery of Britain’s royal family.

Police appear to arrest man after two people stabbed in Golders Green

Fear within the Jewish community in Golders Green is “palpable” after two men were stabbed in the north London area on Wednesday.

The two victims, who have been named as Nachman Moshe ben Chaya Sarah and Moshe Ben Baila, were taken to hospital with knife wounds following the incident on Highfield Avenue.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said: “I cannot tell you how palpable the fear that people there have. They are scared, people saying that being visibly Jewish now is impossible.”

Chief rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis also told reporters that people who are “visibly Jewish” are no longer safe on UK streets.

A terrorist incident has been declared, and a 45-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. He was Tasered after he allegedly tried to stab police officers. The Metropolitan Police said the suspect had a “history of serious violence and mental health issues”.

During a press conference, Met Police chief Sir Mark Rowley was heckled with chants of “resign” and “shame on you”, while prime minister Sir Keir Starmer has called an emergency Cobra meeting.

There has been a string of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in north London. Wednesday’s stabbings took place near where four Jewish ambulances were set on fire in an antisemitic hate crime.

News.title: Trump gives rambling answer on whether Ukraine or Iran war will end first — and confuses the countries
News.content:

President Donald Trump couldn’t say whether the war he launched against Iran in February would end before the four-year-old Russian war against Ukraine — and even confused the two countries — as he turned an Oval Office meeting to honor the Artemis II lunar mission crew into a wide-ranging media session with reporters.

After a spare, two minutes of remarks to honor the NASA crew that traveled further into space than any humans before — during which Trump, 79, claimed he was physically fit enough to launch into deep space as they did (”Is a president allowed to go up in one of these missions,” he asked NASA administrator Jared Isaacman) — the president immediately began a question-and-answer session that veered from UFOs to a recent conversation with Russian president Vladimir Putin that had focused on the Ukraine and Iran wars.

“I talked about Ukraine, and I talked a little bit about Iran. I talked about few different subjects, mostly about Ukraine, and we had a very good conversation. I think we're going to come up with a solution relatively quickly,” he said Wednesday.

Trump said Putin would “like to be involved” with resolving Iran’s possession of enriched uranium — something the United States opposes — and remarked that he’d told Putin in turn that he’d prefer he be “involved with ending the war with Ukraine.”

“He doesn't want to see them have a nuclear weapon either. But I had a long talk with President Putin. I suggested a little bit of a ceasefire. And I think he might do that. He might announce something having to do with that,” Trump said.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump hosted the crew of the NASA Artemis II mission in the Oval Office on Wednesday but spent most of the time veering from UFOs, to Putin, to Iran and Ukraine to former FBI Director James Comey. ( Reuters )

But when pressed further on which of the two wars under discussion would end first, the president said he did not know but called the question “interesting.”

“Which war would end first? I don't know. Maybe they're on a similar timetable,” he said just before confusing Ukraine with Iran as he repeated his oft-used comments that Tehran is “defeated.”

The president also weighed in on the active criminal case against ex-FBI director James Comey, who turned himself in to authorities earlier in the day after a North Carolina grand jury indicted him for allegedly threatening Trump’s life by posting a photo of seashells that spelled out “86 47” to Instagram last year.

The numerical phrase is commonly used in the restaurant industry to indicate that a dish is no longer available or that an intoxicated customer should not be served more alcohol, and Comey has said he meant to indicate that the president should be removed from office.

But the Justice Department alleges that Comey meant it to be an imminent threat against the president’s life, though legal experts have said the charges are unlikely to survive a motion to dismiss because the department’s allegations don’t meet the threshold the Supreme Court has set to bring charges for a threat against the president.

Asked if he believes Comey was truly endangering him, Trump suggested that the term “86” had origins in Italian organized crime as a shorthand for murder.

“You know, you ever see the movies ... the mobster says to one of his wonderful associates, ‘86 him’ — that means, kill him. I think of it as a mob term. I don't know. People think of it as something having to do with disappearing, but the mob uses that term to say, when they want to kill somebody, they say ‘86 the son of a gun,’” he said.

open image in gallery The event was Trump hosting the astronauts but he address Ukraine, Iran, James Comey and a host of other topics ( Reuters )

The president also responded to a reporter question about King Charles III’s remarks to Congress where the royal gave a strong defense of the NATO alliance that Trump has repeatedly denigrated.

Asked if Charles’ speech changed his thinking on the alliance, Trump said he was “very disappointed” because NATO members — including the U.K. — did not join the U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran when it began in February.

But Trump also praised the King as “fantastic” and said he enjoyed his visit with the British monarch.

“We spent a lot of time together. We had a lot of talk ... and he loves his country, and he's a great king, and he's a great friend of mine,” he said.

Trump added that Charles is a “phenomenal representative for his country” of whom the British people “should be proud” and said he “loved” the King’s remarks to Congress — and his subsequent toast at Tuesday night’s White House state dinner.

“I loved his speech yesterday. I watched it. I loved the speech last night. I don't know about my speech. I thought my speech was okay, too, but I thought he was I think he's an unbelievable King, and, by the way, an unbelievable queen,” he said.

The president’s Oval Office appearance was ostensibly to honor the Artemis II crew that circumnavigated the Moon earlier this month.

At the outset of the roughly 20-minute Oval Office appearance, he congratulated them for executing the lunar flyby that was the first trip humans have made there in 53 years while traveling the farthest distance anyone has traveled from Earth.

open image in gallery The Artemis II astronauts took a 10-day journey to the moon and back earlier this month ( Reuters )

“I don’t know how they do it. I wouldn’t want to do it — they have unbelievable courage,” he said as NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, NASA astronauts Christina Koch, Victor Glover, Reid Wiseman and the Canadian Space Agency’s Jeremy Hansen looked on from behind the Resolute desk. The astronauts remained expressionless as Trump answered the various political questions put to him.

The president also joked that he had the chops to become a NASA astronaut himself because one has “to do a lot of things physically good,” which would have given him “no trouble making it.”

Koch and Glover became the first woman and first Black man to reach the moon during their flight earlier this month, which launched from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1 aboard NASA’s Orion spacecraft and the Space Launch System rocket before splashing down in the Pacific off the coast of Southern California on April 10.

During their 10-day journey, they performed science experiments and observed parts of the moon that have never been seen before. The crew even got to name some areas, including a crater they named “Carroll,” as a tribute to Wiseman’s late wife. Carroll Wiseman died from cancer in 2020.

The astronauts are now helping NASA to understand the data they collected on the trip and test out next-generation technology, including improved spacesuits.NASA is working toward launching the next phase of its ambitious Artemis lunar program next year.

During that mission, known as Artemis III, astronauts will test docking capabilities with the spacecraft needed to land on the moon. After that, the space agency is aiming to land astronauts on the lunar surface. The astronauts will explore the moon’s South Pole region. So will NASA drones.

The target date is early 2028 and Trump said he believes NASA has a “good shot.”NASA hopes to eventually set up a permanent base of operations on the moon, including nuclear reactors. From there, the agency will shift its focus to Mars.
